title: Operating Systems I
topics: Role and functions of an operating system

items.q: Which term is described by “hardware that stores and returns data in fixed size chunks, each with its own number”?
o: Interrupt
Device driver
Block device
Arm scheduling
items.s: Block device is hardware that stores and returns data in fixed size chunks, each with its own number.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Mutual exclusion condition for deadlock.
o: the total interval a program spends in the queue without being worked on
the rule that a resource already granted to one program cannot be granted again
the scheme that splits programs into fixed size pages and memory into frames of the same size
the location a program uses, which the hardware translates before reaching the chips
items.s: Mutual exclusion condition for deadlock: the rule that a resource already granted to one program cannot be granted again. The other options describe Logical address, Paging, Waiting time.

items.q: Segmentation may be defined as
o: the hardware location holding the size of the region a program is allowed to touch
the division of a program into variable sized logical parts such as code and data
the record attached to a file naming who may read, write or run it
the placement of a file in one unbroken run of blocks
items.s: Segmentation: the division of a program into variable sized logical parts such as code and data. The other options describe Contiguous allocation, Access control list, Limit register.

items.q: Swapping may be defined as
o: the hardware location holding the size of the region a program is allowed to touch
an operation that changes machine wide settings and is refused to ordinary programs
the moving of a whole program between memory and secondary storage to free room
the standstill in which each of several programs waits for a resource that another of them holds
items.s: Swapping: the moving of a whole program between memory and secondary storage to free room. The other options describe Limit register, Deadlock, Privileged instruction.

items.q: The statement “the fixed interval for which one program is allowed to keep the processor before being moved aside” describes which of the following?
o: Scheduler
Time slice
Priority scheduling
Turnaround time
items.s: Time slice is the fixed interval for which one program is allowed to keep the processor before being moved aside.

items.q: The statement “the restricted state in which ordinary programs run and privileged instructions are refused” describes which of the following?
o: Time sharing
Batch processing
User mode
Supervisor mode
items.s: User mode is the restricted state in which ordinary programs run and privileged instructions are refused.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines File?
o: the division of memory into areas assigned to programs, either fixed in advance or made to fit
the part of a program that touches shared data and must not be entered by two at once
a named collection of related data recorded on storage and handled as one unit
an operation that changes machine wide settings and is refused to ordinary programs
items.s: File: a named collection of related data recorded on storage and handled as one unit. The other options describe Critical section, Partitioning, Privileged instruction.

items.q: Arm scheduling may be defined as
o: the ordering of requests to use a hard disk so that head movement is reduced
the situation in which a ready program is passed over indefinitely because others are always preferred
the rule that runs the ready program with the strongest claim, which can starve weak ones
the part of the system software that decides which program gets the processor, storage and devices
items.s: Arm scheduling: the ordering of requests to use a hard disk so that head movement is reduced. The other options describe Starvation, Resource manager, Priority scheduling.

items.q: Timer interrupt may be defined as
o: the signal from a clock that returns control to the core so one program cannot keep the machine
the total interval a program spends in the queue without being worked on
the running of jobs grouped in advance with no conversation between the user and the machine
the request a running program makes to the core for a service it cannot perform itself
items.s: Timer interrupt: the signal from a clock that returns control to the core so one program cannot keep the machine. The other options describe Waiting time, Batch processing, System call.

items.q: Blocked state may be defined as
o: the writing of intended changes to a log before applying them so a crash can be repaired
the condition of a program that cannot continue until some event such as a completed input finishes
the total interval a program spends in the queue without being worked on
the rule that a resource already granted to one program cannot be granted again
items.s: Blocked state: the condition of a program that cannot continue until some event such as a completed input finishes. The other options describe Journaling, Mutual exclusion condition for deadlock, Waiting time.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Firmware?
o: the rule that a program retains what it already has while asking for resources held elsewhere
the signal from a clock that returns control to the core so one program cannot keep the machine
the record in which the system keeps the identity, state and saved registers of one running program
instructions held in read only memory that start the machine and test its parts
items.s: Firmware: instructions held in read only memory that start the machine and test its parts. The other options describe Possession and request condition, Timer interrupt, Process control block.
items.t: Role and functions of an operating system

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Page table.
o: the structure recording which storage units belong to each stored item and which are free
the route of names from a starting point that leads to one file or folder
the per program structure giving the frame in which each virtual unit currently sits
a single stream of instructions inside a program that shares memory with other such streams
items.s: Page table: the per program structure giving the frame in which each virtual unit currently sits. The other options describe Path, Thread, Allocation map.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Priority scheduling.
o: the rule that runs the ready program with the strongest claim, which can starve weak ones
the software that knows the registers and commands of one particular piece of hardware
the record attached to a file naming who may read, write or run it
the part of the system software that decides which program gets the processor, storage and devices
items.s: Priority scheduling: the rule that runs the ready program with the strongest claim, which can starve weak ones. The other options describe Access control list, Resource manager, Device driver.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Time sharing?
o: the arrangement that lets many users work at terminals together by rapid switching
hardware that stores and returns data in fixed size chunks, each with its own number
the command interpreter through which a user asks the system to carry out work
the part of a program that touches shared data and must not be entered by two at once
items.s: Time sharing: the arrangement that lets many users work at terminals together by rapid switching. The other options describe Block device, Critical section, Shell.

items.q: Which term is described by “the moving of a whole program between memory and secondary storage to free room”?
o: Page table
Segmentation
Swapping
Paging
items.s: Swapping is the moving of a whole program between memory and secondary storage to free room.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Paging?
o: the saving of one program's registers and the restoring of another's so that execution can move between them
the request a running program makes to the core for a service it cannot perform itself
the standstill in which each of several programs waits for a resource that another of them holds
the scheme that splits programs into fixed size pages and memory into frames of the same size
items.s: Paging: the scheme that splits programs into fixed size pages and memory into frames of the same size. The other options describe Deadlock, System call, Context switch.

items.q: Kernel may be defined as
o: the part of a program that touches shared data and must not be entered by two at once
the topmost folder from which every other name in the hierarchy hangs
the resident core of the system software that always holds control of the processor
the event that the unit a program wants is absent from memory, so the core must fetch it
items.s: Kernel: the resident core of the system software that always holds control of the processor. The other options describe Critical section, Root directory, Page fault.
items.t: Role and functions of an operating system

items.q: Program counter may be defined as
o: the register that holds the address of the next instruction to be carried out
the location a program uses, which the hardware translates before reaching the chips
the record attached to a file naming who may read, write or run it
a holding area in memory that evens out the difference in speed between a program and a device
items.s: Program counter: the register that holds the address of the next instruction to be carried out. The other options describe Access control list, Buffer, Logical address.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Monolithic kernel?
o: the writing of intended changes to a log before applying them so a crash can be repaired
the register that holds the address of the next instruction to be carried out
the ordering of requests to use a hard disk so that head movement is reduced
an arrangement in which all core services run together in one privileged program
items.s: Monolithic kernel: an arrangement in which all core services run together in one privileged program. The other options describe Arm scheduling, Journaling, Program counter.

items.q: No preemption condition for deadlock may be defined as
o: the part of a program that touches shared data and must not be entered by two at once
the choice of which held unit to send out when a wanted one must be brought in
the rule that a resource is surrendered only when the holder gives it up voluntarily
the division of memory into areas assigned to programs, either fixed in advance or made to fit
items.s: No preemption condition for deadlock: the rule that a resource is surrendered only when the holder gives it up voluntarily. The other options describe Partitioning, Page replacement policy, Critical section.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Monolithic kernel?
o: the event that the unit a program wants is absent from memory, so the core must fetch it
an arrangement in which all core services run together in one privileged program
the division of a program into variable sized logical parts such as code and data
the interval for the reading head of a hard disk to reach the track holding the wanted data
items.s: Monolithic kernel: an arrangement in which all core services run together in one privileged program. The other options describe Seek time, Segmentation, Page fault.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Arm scheduling?
o: the ordering of requests to use a hard disk so that head movement is reduced
the number of programs completed in a given period
the repeated reading of a device status by the processor instead of being signalled
the rule that gives the processor to whichever program has waited longest
items.s: Arm scheduling: the ordering of requests to use a hard disk so that head movement is reduced. The other options describe Throughput, Polling, First come first served.

items.q: Round robin may be defined as
o: the running of jobs grouped in advance with no conversation between the user and the machine
the location a program uses, which the hardware translates before reaching the chips
the rule that gives each ready program a fixed slice in turn and moves to the back afterwards
the range of memory locations that one program may refer to
items.s: Round robin: the rule that gives each ready program a fixed slice in turn and moves to the back afterwards. The other options describe Batch processing, Logical address, Address space.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Extended machine?
o: the view of the hardware that the system software presents, hiding awkward details behind simple services
the rule that a program retains what it already has while asking for resources held elsewhere
the signal from a clock that returns control to the core so one program cannot keep the machine
an arrangement in which only the least possible service runs privileged and the rest run as ordinary programs
items.s: Extended machine: the view of the hardware that the system software presents, hiding awkward details behind simple services. The other options describe Possession and request condition, Microkernel, Timer interrupt.
items.t: Role and functions of an operating system

items.q: Which term is described by “the view of the hardware that the system software presents, hiding awkward details behind simple services”?
o: Extended machine
Kernel
Shell
Resource manager
items.s: Extended machine is the view of the hardware that the system software presents, hiding awkward details behind simple services.
items.t: Role and functions of an operating system

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Time slice.
o: the rule that picks the ready program needing the least processor time to finish
the rule that runs the ready program with the strongest claim, which can starve weak ones
the running of jobs grouped in advance with no conversation between the user and the machine
the fixed interval for which one program is allowed to keep the processor before being moved aside
items.s: Time slice: the fixed interval for which one program is allowed to keep the processor before being moved aside. The other options describe Priority scheduling, Batch processing, Shortest job first.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Path.
o: the placement of a file in one unbroken run of blocks
the route of names from a starting point that leads to one file or folder
a program in execution together with the state of its registers, memory and open resources
the rule that gives each ready program a fixed slice in turn and moves to the back afterwards

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Starvation.
o: the record in which the system keeps the identity, state and saved registers of one running program
the situation in which a ready program is passed over indefinitely because others are always preferred
a program in execution together with the state of its registers, memory and open resources
the per program structure giving the frame in which each virtual unit currently sits
items.s: Starvation: the situation in which a ready program is passed over indefinitely because others are always preferred. The other options describe Process, Page table, Process control block.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines User mode?
o: the restricted state in which ordinary programs run and privileged instructions are refused
the transfer of data between a device and main storage without the processor copying each item
instructions held in read only memory that start the machine and test its parts
the arrangement that lets many users work at terminals together by rapid switching
items.s: User mode: the restricted state in which ordinary programs run and privileged instructions are refused. The other options describe Time sharing, Direct memory access, Firmware.

items.q: First come first served may be defined as
o: the topmost folder from which every other name in the hierarchy hangs
the part of a program that touches shared data and must not be entered by two at once
the signal that makes the processor set aside what it is doing and serve a device
the rule that gives the processor to whichever program has waited longest
items.s: First come first served: the rule that gives the processor to whichever program has waited longest. The other options describe Interrupt, Critical section, Root directory.

items.q: The statement “the unrestricted state in which the core runs and every instruction is allowed” describes which of the following?
o: Timer interrupt
Supervisor mode
Time sharing
Microkernel
items.s: Supervisor mode is the unrestricted state in which the core runs and every instruction is allowed.

items.q: All of the following belong to Processes and the processor EXCEPT
o: Program counter
Process
Process control block
Fragmentation
items.s: Every other option belongs to Processes and the processor. “Fragmentation” belongs to Memory management, not Processes and the processor.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Mounting?
o: the placement of a file in one unbroken run of blocks
the record in which the system keeps the identity, state and saved registers of one running program
the attaching of a storage device into the existing folder hierarchy so its contents appear there
a holding area in memory that evens out the difference in speed between a program and a device
items.s: Mounting: the attaching of a storage device into the existing folder hierarchy so its contents appear there. The other options describe Process control block, Buffer, Contiguous allocation.

items.q: Which term is described by “the command interpreter through which a user asks the system to carry out work”?
o: Utility program
Shell
System call
Kernel
items.s: Shell is the command interpreter through which a user asks the system to carry out work.

items.q: The statement “the act of making a new unit of execution, often by copying an existing one” describes which of the following?
o: Blocked state
Process creation
Process
Process termination
items.s: Process creation is the act of making a new unit of execution, often by copying an existing one.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Thread?
o: the ending of a unit of execution and the release of what it held
the sequence that loads the core into memory when the machine is switched on
a single stream of instructions inside a program that shares memory with other such streams
the moving of a whole program between memory and secondary storage to free room
items.s: Thread: a single stream of instructions inside a program that shares memory with other such streams. The other options describe Process termination, Booting, Swapping.

items.q: The statement “the record attached to a file naming who may read, write or run it” describes which of the following?
o: Access control list
File
Contiguous allocation
Path

the signal from a clock that returns control to the core so one program cannot keep the machine

items.q: The statement “the transfer of data between a device and main storage without the processor copying each item” describes which of the following?
o: Seek time
Buffer
Interrupt
Direct memory access

items.q: Partitioning may be defined as

the rule that gives each ready program a fixed slice in turn and moves to the back afterwards
a named collection of related data recorded on storage and handled as one unit

items.q: The statement “the attaching of a storage device into the existing folder hierarchy so its contents appear there” describes which of the following?

Mounting
Directory
items.s: Mounting is the attaching of a storage device into the existing folder hierarchy so its contents appear there.

the restricted state in which ordinary programs run and privileged instructions are refused
the rule that gives the processor to whichever program has waited longest

o: the loading of program parts only as needed so a small machine runs a large job
the record in which the system keeps the identity, state and saved registers of one running program
the shifting of allocated areas together to gather the free space into one block
a single stream of instructions inside a program that shares memory with other such streams

the condition of a program that could run at once and is only waiting for the processor
the rule that picks the ready program needing the least processor time to finish
the record in which the system keeps the identity, state and saved registers of one running program
items.s: Process control block: the record in which the system keeps the identity, state and saved registers of one running program. The other options describe Shortest job first, Ready state, Utility program.

the rule that runs the ready program with the strongest claim, which can starve weak ones
the division of a program into variable sized logical parts such as code and data
the rule that a resource is surrendered only when the holder gives it up voluntarily
items.s: Shortest job first: the rule that picks the ready program needing the least processor time to finish. The other options describe Priority scheduling, No preemption condition for deadlock, Segmentation.

the saving of one program's registers and the restoring of another's so that execution can move between them
the register that holds the address of the next instruction to be carried out
the sequence that loads the core into memory when the machine is switched on
items.s: Supervisor mode: the unrestricted state in which the core runs and every instruction is allowed. The other options describe Booting, Program counter, Context switch.

items.s: Least recently used is the replacement rule that sends out the page that has gone longest without being touched.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the command interpreter through which a user asks the system to carry out work”
o: Shell
Kernel
Booting
Resource manager
items.s: Shell is the command interpreter through which a user asks the system to carry out work.
items.t: Role and functions of an operating system

items.q: In this course, Overlay refers to
o: the shifting of allocated areas together to gather the free space into one block
the loading of program parts only as needed so a small machine runs a large job
the location a program uses, which the hardware translates before reaching the chips
the division of memory into areas assigned to programs, either fixed in advance or made to fit
items.s: Overlay: the loading of program parts only as needed so a small machine runs a large job. The other options describe Partitioning, Logical address, Compaction.

items.q: “the range of memory locations that one program may refer to” is the definition of
o: Partitioning
Address space
Base register
Compaction
items.s: Address space is the range of memory locations that one program may refer to.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Priority scheduling.
o: the number of programs completed in a given period
the total interval a program spends in the queue without being worked on
the rule that runs the ready program with the strongest claim, which can starve weak ones
the situation in which a ready program is passed over indefinitely because others are always preferred
items.s: Priority scheduling: the rule that runs the ready program with the strongest claim, which can starve weak ones. The other options describe Throughput, Starvation, Waiting time.

items.q: The correct meaning of Process creation is
o: the condition of a program that could run at once and is only waiting for the processor
the record in which the system keeps the identity, state and saved registers of one running program
the act of making a new unit of execution, often by copying an existing one
the register that holds the address of the next instruction to be carried out
items.s: Process creation: the act of making a new unit of execution, often by copying an existing one. The other options describe Ready state, Process control block, Program counter.
